In these cases, ChaaS providers purchase and install EVSE at the site of the user and serve as a “middleperson” between the user and the electricity provider. There are many reasons for the popularity of this emerging model, but most of the recent marketing materials for these models emphasize their role in streamlining and speeding the design, installation, and maintenance of EVSE, and reducing up-front costs24. A recent review of charging infrastructure business models25 offers a categorization of roles served by public EV charging networks for light-duty transportation, but does not call explicit attention to the role of ChaaS provider. The review highlights the need to assign clear roles among owners, hosts, operators, and other entities in the EV charging system to enable large-scale EV adoption, and raises the timely question of whether infrastructure deployment is a public or private responsibility. In this work, we offer a comprehensive definition of the role of ChaaS provider, and we find ChaaS to be a flexible means for directing public and/or private investments toward the efficient rollout of charging infrastructure.
